[[File:Studium der Pharmazie, Kairo 1959 und 1960, v.l.n.r..jpg|thumb|Studies of pharmacy, Cairo 1959 and 1960]]
'''Ahmed Hegazy''' (also: Hegasy; Arabic [[أحمد حجازي]], Aḥmad Ḥiǧāzī, born October 24, 1939, in Cairo; died February 5, 2021, in [[Leverkusen]]) was an Egyptian-German pharmacist. He conducted research in the Pharmaceutical Technology Department of [[Bayer]] from 1966 to 1999, during which time he invented a new galenic formulation for the active components [[nifedipine]] and [[nimodipine]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Solid, rapidly released medicament preparations containing dihydropyridines, and processes for their preparation|url=https://uspto.report/patent/grant/4,981,683|access-date=2022-02-05|website=USPTO.report|language=en}}</ref>{{Medical citation needed|date=June 2024}} By blocking calcium channels, the substance has a relaxing effect on vascular muscles and is therefore used for the treatment of [[hypertension]].{{Medical citation needed|date=June 2024}} In 1991, Hegazy received the [https://www.bayer.com/en/innovation/otto-bayer-medal Otto Bayer Medal] for the solubilization of poorly soluble ingredients such as nimodipine.{{Medical citation needed|date=June 2024}} His galenic invention is still the basis for many modern formulations at Bayer AG (A. Ohm).{{Medical citation needed|date=June 2024}}

== Life ==
{{Unreferenced section|date=June 2024}}
[[File:Letter Dr Knut Schauerte, patent rights Adalat, 1987.pdf|thumb|Letter Dr K. Schauerte, patent rights Adalat, 1987. Source: Family archive.{{Primary source inline|reason=purported patent letter source is an unknown and unverified source|date=June 2024}}]]
Ahmed Hegazy was born in Cairo in 1939 as the youngest of seven siblings. As shown in his high school diploma, he passed the matriculation examination in 1955 in the natural sciences branch as 296th out of 10,445 students. After studying pharmacy at [[Cairo University]], he was sent to West Germany in 1961 by a [[United Arab Republic]] study mission on a scholarship for a Ph.D. at the [[Technical University of Braunschweig]]. In 1966, he received his doctorate supervised by [[:de:Walther Awe|Walther Awe]] with a thesis on "Contributions to the analytics of pantothenic acid and pantothenol." Since 1966, he worked at Bayer in Leverkusen, first as plant manager at the penicillin factory, then as laboratory manager in galenics and finally as head of department in the Institute for Pharmaceutical Technology for Liquid and Semi-Solid Pharmaceutical Forms. From 1977 onward he researched the administration of nifedipine, which brought the drug to world market maturity under the name ''Adalat retard''. In his spare time, he was a passionate botanist. He retired in 1999 and died in Leverkusen in 2021.

== Work ==
{{Unreferenced medical section|date=June 2024}}
[[File:Urkunde Otto-Bayer-Medaille für galenische Erfindung Copräzipitat.jpg|thumb|Award certificate Otto-Bayer prize, 1991{{Primary source inline|reason=purported award letter source is an unknown and unverified source|date=June 2024}}]]
On September 9, 1980, Bayer patented a solid drug preparation containing nifedipine for Ahmed Hegazy and Klaus-Dieter Rämsch at the [[German Patent Office]] in Munich (No. DE3033919 and EP0047899).<ref>{{Cite web|last1=Hegasy|first1=Ahmed|last2=Rämsch|first2=Klaus-Dieter|date=28 February 1996|title=Solid pharmaceutical compositions containing nifedipine, and process for their preparation|url=https://patentimages.storage.googleapis.com/8c/e7/6b/65e124ccf4f4bd/EP0047899B2.pdf|access-date=29 January 2022|website=Patentimages}}</ref>{{Failed verification|date=June 2024|reason=percentage of patent assignment not in cited source}} The surface area of 1–4 m<sup>2</sup>/g resulted in the best absorption effect and a release over up to 36h.{{Medical citation needed|date=June 2024}} Previously, nifedipine was administered as a soft [[gelatin]] capsule. This was very light-sensitive and could not be manufactured by the company itself.{{Medical citation needed|date=June 2024}} The production of the  capsules had to be outsourced to the company [[R.P. Scherer Corporation|R.P. Scherer]].{{Citation needed|date=June 2024}} In addition, the gelatin shell contained pork skins and could thus not be exported worldwide. The ''Adalat retard'' tablet, on the other hand, used iron oxide as light protection.{{Medical citation needed|date=June 2024}} The Bayer AG secured the patent in more than 40 countries.{{Citation needed|date=June 2024}} 
[[File:Umsatz Adalat 1975-1992 weltweit.jpg|thumb|Sales Adalat and Adalat retard globally between 1975 and 1992{{Primary source inline|reason=purported sales figures source is an unknown and unverified source|date=June 2024}}]]
In the 1990s ''Adalat'' replaced ''[[Aspirin]]'' as the Bayer Group's largest single product for two reasons:<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=NjPvBgAAQBAJ|title=Pharma-Unternehmen und Gesundheitsmanagement: Strategische Diversifizierung durch Dienstleistungen|date=2013-07-02|publisher=Springer-Verlag|isbn=978-3-322-99515-5|language=de}}</ref> The expansion of the indication to include hypertension in 1985, and a once-a-day regimen{{Medical citation needed|date=June 2024}} due to the invention of the retard tablet. Both led to substantive increase in global sales.<ref>{{Cite web|title=File:Adalat Umsatz 1992 in Mio DM.pdf - Wikipedia|url=https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Adalat_Umsatz_1992_in_Mio_DM.pdf|access-date=2022-01-29|website=commons.wikimedia.org|date=29 January 2022 |language=en}}</ref>{{Primary source inline|reason=purported sale figures source is an unknown and unverified source|date=June 2024}} By 2001, turnover had risen to €975 mio.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2002|title=Bayer Annual Report 2001|url=https://www.annualreports.com/HostedData/AnnualReportArchive/b/OTC_BAYZF_2001.pdf|access-date=5 February 2022|website=Annualreports|pages=8–9}}</ref> The rise of ''Adalat retard'' after 1990 is a paradigmatic case for the success of already established medication due to new forms of administration{{Medical citation needed|date=June 2024}} "even though the drug had already been on the market for a quarter of a century," writes a study by the [[University of Applied Sciences Erfurt|Erfurt University of Applied Sciences]] on.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Mey |first=Alexander |date=2013 |title=Rx-to-OTC-Switch als strategischer Ansatz im Life-Cycle-Management für pharmazeutische Produkte |url=https://www.db-thueringen.de/servlets/MCRFileNodeServlet/dbt_derivate_00043994/Heft40Pharmamarketingkomplett%20A.pdf |journal=Erfurter Hefte zum Angewandten Marketing |language=German |publisher=Fachhochschule Erfurt University of Applied Sciences Wirtschafts-wissenschaften |volume=40 |page=17}}</ref> Today, it is still one of Bayer's 15 most important pharmaceutical products.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Bayer AG - Umsatz der Top Pharma-Produkte 2021|url=https://de.statista.com/statistik/daten/studie/20066/umfrage/umsatz-der-top-pharma-produkte-der-bayer-ag/|access-date=2022-01-29|website=Statista|language=de}}</ref> In a legal dispute between Bayer and [[Pfizer]] in the US in 1995, it was established that Pfizer's product Procardia XL was based on this patent (Patent No. [https://patentimages.storage.googleapis.com/80/e0/2f/1e0ab56b05b557/US5264446.pdf US5264446]).{{Failed verification|date=June 2024|reason=patent lawsuit, Hegazy, attorney Schauerte all not mentioned in the cited source at all, none at all}} Ahmed Hegazy was involved in ten other patents of the Bayer group.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Ahmed Hegasy Inventions, Patents and Patent Applications - Justia Patents Search|url=https://patents.justia.com/inventor/ahmed-hegasy|access-date=2022-02-05|website=patents.justia.com}}</ref>{{Failed verification|date=June 2024|reason=patent lawsuit, Hegazy, attorney Schauerte all not mentioned in the cited source at all, none at all}}
